deckName: KS3 DT · J2 Lesson 5 — Loop Machines (Teacher Deck)

slides.kicker: OUR LADY'S GRAMMAR SCHOOL · DIGITAL TECHNOLOGY
slides.heading: Lesson 5 · Loop Machines
slides.notes:
WHERE THE CLASS IS: the class is coming in, logging in and opening the class link. The lesson opens on the Do-Now. This is three questions from earlier lessons, and they mark themselves. Take the register while the class works on it.

SAY: "Today is Lesson 5, Loop Machines. Log in, open the class link, and work through the three questions. When they are done, stop and look up."

DO NOT describe what comes after the Do-Now. What pupils meet on screen is meant to be a surprise, so say nothing about it beyond these slides.

slides.heading: Today you meet loops
bullets: A loop makes the computer do the same job many times.
You write the job once, then say how many times.
You will also meet a counter called i. You will also meet three bugs, which are mistakes in a program.
slides.notes: SAY these as they are written. Do not explain loops now: the lesson explains each idea just before you use it.

slides.heading: Headphones on
bullets: Sound is part of this lesson. Put your headphones on now.
The lesson works with the sound off too. Every sound is shown as a picture on the screen.
Sound turns on the first time you click a button. Until then, nothing makes a sound.
slides.notes: SAY: "Headphones on now, please. Sound is part of today. If you have no headphones, everything still works with the sound off."

slides.heading: On your own
bullets: You work on your own screen at your own speed. You do not wait for anyone, and no one waits for you.
Every program you type really runs. If it is wrong, the screen tells you what it did and what to change.
If you need to leave the room, click Pause at the bottom left of your screen. It stops everything.
slides.notes: SAY: "Today you work on your own, at your own speed. Every program you type really runs. If your program is wrong, the screen tells you what it did and what to change. If you need to leave the room, click Pause before you go."

slides.heading: Read every screen
bullets: Every screen tells you one thing. Read it, then click Next.
When it says type, type all the lines. Then click Run.
If something goes wrong, read the yellow sentence. It tells you the fix.
slides.notes: SAY: "Read before you type. Nothing moves on until you click Next."

slides.heading: Click Start the hour on your screen
bullets: Open the class link and click Start the hour.
If you need to leave the room, click Pause at the bottom left of your screen.
If your screen says “Running out of time”, finish the chapter you are on and click Home.
slides.notes:
SAY it once: "Open the class link and click Start the hour. If you need to leave the room, click Pause. If your screen says “Running out of time”, finish the chapter you are on and click Home."

THEN: say nothing until the last screens. Walk around the room. A stuck pupil's screen names the fix in one sentence. After two wrong tries it circles the exact lines on the pupil's screen. A pupil who is quiet and typing is working.

slides.heading: The last screens
bullets: First you answer five questions. Then you fill in the screen called “How did it go?”
If there is time, you can do the part called Free flight. You can keep going until the bell.
slides.notes: SAY: "At the end there are five questions, then the screen called How did it go? Everybody does both. If there is time after that, you can use Free flight until the bell."

slides.heading: Before you leave
bullets: Finish the screen called “How did it go?” Nobody leaves until it is done.
Sign out before you leave the computer.
Your place is saved. Do not tell other classes what happens in the story. They have not played it yet.
slides.notes: SAY the sign-out line every lesson without exception. On shared C2k machines it is the single habit that matters most. Remind them to keep today a surprise for other classes.
